purposeAndStandards.mission: Issue accurate proof of insurance within agency timelines while ensuring every certificate reflects verified policy coverage, forms, endorsements, and authorized client instructions.

standardsOfSuccess.name: Written, timely service
standardsOfSuccess.description: Obtain the request in writing, apply the Certificate of Insurance label, process within one hour, and document the required phone, email, and text outreach.

standardsOfSuccess.name: Coverage-first accuracy
standardsOfSuccess.description: Verify policy status, forms, endorsements, holder information, red flags, and master-certificate data before preparing or issuing proof.

standardsOfSuccess.name: Complete digital delivery
standardsOfSuccess.description: Issue through EZLynx and Client Center, attach all required forms, educate clients on self-service access, and maintain the pending-certificate trackers.

ezlynxAndFileStandards.folder: Create a separate folder for each Certificate Master

nonNegotiables.detail: Do not issue when coverage, policy status, written-contract conditions, forms, or red-flag requirements are deficient or unresolved; route the file to the Account Manager.

nonNegotiables.rule: Never misstate or duplicate certificate data
nonNegotiables.detail: Use the full legal certificate-holder name when known, avoid duplicate holders, update master remarks and endorsements, and require policy changes to be entered in EZLynx first.
Do not accept oral-only requests, omit attachments or notes, skip Client Center education, ignore tracker status, or issue after a required escalation without approval.

step1_Verify.role: CSR / Technician; assign coverage interpretation, deficiencies, red flags, and exceptions to the Producer / Account Manager or team lead.
actions: Obtain the certificate request in writing, confirm current contact information, verify all policy statuses, apply the Certificate of Insurance label, and follow the EZLynx checklist.

Confirm that the insured has the exact coverage and forms requested. Common items include Additional Insured; completed and ongoing operations; primary and non-contributory; waiver of subrogation; CG 2010/CG 2037; action-over or labor-law restrictions; hired/non-owned or Any Auto; 30-day cancellation notice; designated premises; and classification limitations.

Review contractors/commercial red flags: New York work and wording, action-over/employee-injury exclusions, snow removal, roofing, tree removal, foundation repair, house raising, underground work, named-insured requirements, and event or one-day-event exposures.

Review trucking red flags: unlimited radius, towing, physical damage, pollution cleanup, hired/non-owned or Any Auto, seafood, UIIA, alcohol, steel beams/coils, and any required special cargo. Check with Mike Sosa on UIIA.

Document every verification, red flag, and carrier communication. If anything is deficient, if a required policy change is not fully entered in EZLynx, or if coverage cannot be verified, do not issue; notify the agent and team lead and reassign to the Account Manager. Log data-integrity violations on the daily report.

step2_Prepare.role: CSR / Technician; involve the Account Manager for unprocessed changes, renewal approval, reinstatement confirmation, or unavailable coverage/forms.

scenarios.newPolicy: Create a new master COI; select the correct master remarks and coverage endorsements; attach required policy forms and vehicle schedule; add ACORD 101; and enable Client Center.
scenarios.policyChange: If the change has not been processed, assign to the Account Manager. When complete, edit the master COI, attach required forms, and add ACORD 101 when a new master is created; a routine holder does not require a new ACORD 101.
scenarios.cancellationReinstatementRewrite: For near-cancellation, issue only through the cancellation expiration date. For a cancelled policy, use the approved cancellation template. For reinstatement, issue only after carrier or MGA confirmation—not finance-company confirmation. Add ACORD 101 when creating a new master.
scenarios.additionalPolicy: Create the new master, add remarks/forms/vehicle schedule/ACORD 101, import holders from the old master, mark the old master Do Not Use, disable its Client Center access, and enable Client Center on the new master.
scenarios.renewal: If the renewal is in EZLynx, use the Renewal function to import holders and verify coverage. If not, build a renewal-term master, import holders, and disable the old master. Issue only after payment/EFT confirmation on the carrier site or Account Manager approval; add forms, vehicle schedule, ACORD 101, and Client Center.
scenarios.masterDataStandards: Use the certificate holder’s full legal name when known; otherwise follow the written request and use the suggested EZLynx address when appropriate. Do not duplicate holders; update the existing database record and master remarks.

step3_Issue.role: CSR / Technician; obtain Producer / Account Manager approval whenever requested wording or proof could expand, interpret, or misrepresent coverage.
actions: Issue through EZLynx using the on-behalf-of function, send from Certificates, copy the insured, follow the agency naming convention, and deliver through Client Center. Use the approved Proof of Insurance Delivery template.

Use general wording for Additional Insured and Waiver of Subrogation references. Attach the actual AI/WOS endorsements every time and cite the form number in Description of Operations. Handle PAC forms case by case.
Update the COI Forms Tracker and the Pending COIs/Endorsements tracker for open work. If a certificate remains pending over seven days, follow the Carlo escalation rule in What Ifs.

Certificate Party Definitions: • Additional insured: receives certain liability protection under an endorsement. • Mortgagee, loss payee, lienholder, or leasing company: has a financial interest in covered property or a vehicle.

Subcontractor COI Check: • Match required limits and confirm ongoing/completed operations, project details, waiver of subrogation, primary/noncontributory wording, workers’ compensation limits, and commercial auto requirements when applicable.

whatIfs.rule: Break out General Liability, on-hook cargo, and physical damage separately on the master COI even when they share one Progressive policy.
Obtain the insured’s approval before issuing a certificate on the insured’s behalf.
Verify that the required written contract or other endorsement condition applies before issuing. If it does not, do not issue.
Confirm with the owner that the person may be added, create the contact in Details, enable Client Center, and send the approved Certificate Self Service completion communication.
Use the correct coverage identifiers: AL for auto liability, APD for auto physical damage, and MTC for motor truck cargo.
Keep separate masters when distinct operations or policies cannot fit the main master, such as snowplow or fidelity coverage; select the correct master for the request.
Obtain team-lead approval and use the Quick Proof of Insurance Change Requests guidance before issuing.

whatIfs.topic: Carrier Website Is Inaccessible or Unfamiliar
whatIfs.rule: Alert the team lead for assistance. Do not issue unverified information.
Explain that email and Client Center are preferred. Mail the documents as a courtesy through the approved EZLynx Postal Mail workflow while onboarding the client to digital service.
Verify the General Liability limitations and check for an inland-marine endorsement. Obtain year, make, serial number, value, and equipment type before preparing proof.
Use Postal Mail when severity warrants it and document the open requirement and contact attempts.
Use Postal Mail, send the approved bad-contact memo, and update verified contact details.

Contact by email, text, and phone, set expectations upfront, and document with Labels. If the insured remains unresponsive, notify the carrier, send any severity-based Postal Mail, and close according to the carrier’s direction.
Notify the team lead and document the escalation.

whatIfs.topic: No Documentation from a Non-Downloading Carrier
whatIfs.rule: Contact the carrier and team lead. Do not issue until adequate carrier documentation is available.
Issue the certificate when the insured specifically requests informational-only proof, while keeping all policy-governs wording and verified coverage limits intact.
Document the defect, create a new master certificate, complete a quality check, and notify Carlo.
Obtain Account Manager review, temporarily update the master to the approved physical address, issue the COI, then restore the mailing address on the master.
Email underwriting3@guard.com to obtain the form because it is not available online.
Use the binder to create the shell policy while waiting for download. For manually entered policies, use the binder when the declarations page or full policy has not arrived so proof is not delayed.
Save the request email to EZLynx through Gmail and reassign it to the CSR.

Immediately alert Carlo, contact the insured using the approved pending dropdown templates, and close only after the insured says the certificate is no longer needed or after a no-response closure notice is sent.

robieSkillGuidance.subcontractorCOICheck: Match limits, ongoing/completed operations, project details, waiver of subrogation, primary/noncontributory wording, WC limits, and commercial auto.
escalationHelpTriggers: Request is oral-only, incomplete, or contact information cannot be verified.
Coverage, forms, endorsements, written-contract conditions, or policy status cannot be verified.
Red flags, special wording, or requested proof could expand, interpret, or misrepresent coverage.
Required policy change is not fully entered in EZLynx.
Cancellation, reinstatement, rewrite, or renewal payment/EFT confirmation is unclear (never rely solely on finance-company confirmation).
Carrier website is inaccessible/unfamiliar, or documentation from a non-downloading carrier is missing.
Existing master is incorrect, rush request needs team-lead approval, or certificate remains pending over seven days (Carlo escalation rule).
Any instruction conflicts with Core Rules, Agency Standards, or Primary SOP.
